key_insight: Fe or Cr substitution at Ni grain-boundary planes increases cohesion, with strengthening dependent on element type and local structure.
engineering_relevance: Atomistically predicted separation energies and peak tractions can inform continuum fracture models for multicomponent Ni-based alloys.
method: Compute DFT rigid-body separation curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni grain boundaries.
Extract work of separation and maximum traction using the universal binding energy relation.
Benchmark ML interatomic potentials against DFT, then sample finer alloying increments and a ternary composition.
evidence_signal: One tested ML potential quantitatively reproduced DFT separation energies and peak tractions; calculations also examined ternary Ni56Fe20Cr24.
watch_item: Binary alloying trends do not quantitatively capture Fe–Cr interplay, so explicit ternary calculations remain necessary.
paper_title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
